title: Institutional Authority and Governed Continuity in Mindful Machine Architecture
content: Enterprise agentic AI requires an architecture that preserves institutional authority while models, tools, and execution resources change. This article develops the Mindful Machine as a governance-native process architecture in which a ratified Digital Genome specifies purpose, delegated authority, constraints, expected consequences, and recovery duties. The Autopoietic and Metacognitive Orchestration System executes declared governance processes; consequential actions require bounded Authorization Warrants; and an episode of record links proposals, decisions, effects, observations, obligations, and accountable closure. Eight properties make the architecture testable: purpose governance, authority separation, continuity preservation, consequence grounding, human-accountable closure, self-regulation, causal memory, and substrate independence. A conditional argument establishes commitment admission under explicit enforcement assumptions, while a conformance method separates architectural requirements from implementation evidence. Published video-streaming and credit-default implementations establish a broader engineering lineage; governed account recovery illustrates consequence recording and closure; and 25 synthetic prior-authorization records contain 10 accepted, 3 denied, and 12 escalated dispositions. These implementations provide existence evidence for reusable mechanisms rather than a universal assurance claim. The contribution is a coherent specification of authority custody and commitment-aware continuity across heterogeneous workflows, together with falsifiable requirements for evaluating its realizations.
